transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Time: 14:00 PT / 17:00 ET
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Hale (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Atlas Procurement), Jonas Meyer (Atlas InfoSec), Sarah Cole (Atlas Cloud Ops), Markus Lind (Atlas Legal)

Summary: Quick procurement intake focused on SLA tiering distinctions (hosted vs dedicated), potential data transfer/egress fee models, and how exceptions in the MSA/DPA for cross-border or FedRAMP-impacting clauses should be handled. Agreed next steps include sending annotated MSA/DPA, running a Dedicated benchmark, and circling legal for redlines.

Topics: SLA brackets, pricing worksheet (committed levels), data residency & egress, KMS/HSM options, audit log retention, DPA exceptions, PO path and billing cadence.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Lena, AE on the Redwood side. Marcus is our systems engineer who will cover the benchmark and the KMS details.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Hi, Priya here, procurement. We're doing intake to figure out the approval path — particularly pricing approver and any legal exceptions that will slow us down.
[00:28] Jonas Meyer: Jonas, InfoSec. We'll need clarity on audit logs, retention, and any SOC2 / FedRAMP implications.
[00:34] Marcus Hale: Marcus, hey — I'll be your technical point for benchmarks and deployment modes.
[00:40] Sarah Cole: Sarah, cloud ops — interested in egress numbers and how the bill shows up in our Azure account.
[00:46] Markus Lind: Markus, legal — I'll look at the MSA/DPA redlines.

[02:05] Lena Ortiz: Great. The agenda is short — SLA tiers and where pricing breaks, DPA/MSA edge cases for cross-border, and KMS options. If we hit a point that needs follow-up we'll note it as an action.

[03:12] Priya Nair: First, pricing committee wants to see committed vs burst tiers — like if we commit to a monthly reserved GB-hours or vGPU hours, what discounting and SLAs come with it. Also, is there a data transfer or egress fee we should budget?
[03:30] Marcus Hale: Short answer: yes there are egress counters in certain topologies. For hosted API, outbound tokens / payload egress is metered as part of the usage pricing we've put in the sheet. For Dedicated, if you colocate in a VPC peering setup there's often cross-region egress depending on topology — we can model that per your region.

[04:05] Jonas Meyer: Can you be specific? Our legal flagged any per-GB export fee as a blocker unless it's predictable.
[04:14] Lena Ortiz: Understood. We typically provide 3 pricing profiles: self-serve hosted (pay-as-you-go), committed Dedicated (reserved capacity with a predictable monthly invoice), and Private (VPC/on-prem) where we add a platform fee and network egress is customer-managed. The pricing worksheet Marcus will share breaks down committed discounts at 50/70/80% tiers based on commit size.

[05:02] Marcus Hale: We can show two models for egress: 1) included in committed tier up to X TB/month, after that per-GB rates; 2) pass-through billing where you pay cloud egress directly if you're in a private VPC. For example in EU-West, inter-region egress can be material — we recommend pinning region to avoid cross-border costs.

[06:20] Sarah Cole: So if we provision Dedicated in eu-west-1 will cross-Azure traffic to our DC be billed by you?
[06:27] Marcus Hale: If you use our managed VPC peering, Redwood's invoice includes the model compute and our platform fee; the raw cloud egress is usually included up to the committed cap. If you instead deploy Private with customer-managed peering, you incur cloud provider egress directly.

[07:05] Jonas Meyer: For our audit, we need to know log retention and fields. Does Redwood provide immutable audit logs and can we set retention windows beyond 90 days?
[07:17] Marcus Hale: Yes, we provide audit logs of API calls, token usage, and operator actions. Retention is configurable as an add-on — default 90 days, can be extended to 1 year or more with the enterprise package. Logs can be forwarded to your Splunk/Datadog or S3 bucket. There's also an option to sign an SLA for log delivery windows.

[08:40] Markus Lind: On the MSA/DPA: cross-border data transfers are sensitive. Atlas requires explicit padd clauses for transfer outside EEA unless an SCC baseline is used. Does Redwood have standard SCC language or would you accept a specific carve-out?
[08:56] Lena Ortiz: We include standard SCCs in the DPA for EU customers. If you have additional restrictions (no transfers to US unless anonymized) that's an exception we should capture now — we'll circulate an annotated DPA indicating where those redlines would land.

[10:12] Priya Nair: Also procurement wants to know if there's a PO and billing cadence requirement — monthly vs annual? Our finance prefers annual commitments for committed discounts.
[10:22] Lena Ortiz: Annual committed invoices are standard for Dedicated reserved contracts. We support monthly billing for hosted/consumption and annual prepay for reserved capacity — the pricing worksheet will show effective rates.

[11:05] Jonas Meyer: Encryption — we require customer-managed keys for at-rest and an HSM-backed KMS. Is that possible?
[11:13] Marcus Hale: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). For Dedicated/private we can support HSM-backed keys — you can supply the key material or manage keys via your cloud KMS. For hosted public tier, CMKs are supported under enterprise plans with KMS rotation policies.

[12:44] Sarah Cole: Does key access require special entitlements? Who in Redwood has access to key metadata?
[12:50] Marcus Hale: Redwood never stores raw key material; we maintain key references and access is RBAC-controlled. Only designated platform ops runbooks can request key operations during recovery and such are logged. We can provide a runbook for your security team.

[14:10] Lena Ortiz: Quick pivot to SLA tiers — our baseline SLA is 99.9 for hosted; for Dedicated we can offer 99.95 or 99.99 depending on commit and topologies. Higher SLAs include service credits and a playbook for incident escalations.

[14:46] Markus Lind: Service credits — legal will want the formula and any materiality caps. We usually can't accept broad liability.
[14:53] Lena Ortiz: Understandable. Our standard is a sliding credit: X% of monthly fees per hour of downtime beyond the SLA, capped at Y% of the monthly invoice. We'll include the exact formula in the MSA appendix.

[15:30] Jonas Meyer: What's considered downtime for inference? A per-request latency spike vs full model unavailability?
[15:40] Marcus Hale: Good question — downtime is defined as an inability to successfully complete requests to the API endpoints (5xx errors or connection refusal). Latency crossing a threshold is an SLO/latency degradation, which we monitor via observable dashboards but is not always SLA downtime. We can negotiate latency SLOs in the Dedicated contract.

[16:55] Priya Nair: Pricing approvers will ask: if we commit to 3 months then ramp, can we adjust commit mid-term?
[17:04] Lena Ortiz: Commit levels are flexible but discount tiers are based on the committed amount for the invoice period. We offer mid-term top-ups (add capacity) but discounts are based on prorated commits. We'll put those examples in the pricing sheet.

[18:20] Sarah Cole: Are there additional charges for prefix/KV cache warmups or persistent state? Our workloads rely on long context and KV caching — wondering if there's special storage charges.
[18:31] Marcus Hale: KV cache persistence is included in Dedicated — heavy stateful caching at volume could carry a storage surcharge. We'll profile your workload in the benchmark to surface any such costs.

[19:55] Lena Ortiz: Quick legal flags — Markus, any initial redlines you need immediately to surface?
[20:01] Markus Lind: The usual: liability caps, indemnities, data residency, and audit rights. Also want a clear escalation timeline and SLAs for incident response. I'll send a prioritized list after.

[21:22] Marcus Hale: For the benchmark we propose using a 48-hour window of representative requests — we'll generate a synthetic load-close mimic of your token distribution. We'll capture p99 latency, tail latencies, token/sec, and memory/KV miss rates.

[21:50] Jonas Meyer: We can't supply PII for the test. Can you anonymize?
[21:58] Marcus Hale: Absolutely. We'll use synthetic data or de-identified payloads — we'll share the test harness in GitHub and you can run an initial dry run.

[23:05] Priya Nair: On procurement path: who signs the MSA? Are we looking at Redwood legal or an authorized Redwood sig on the order form?
[23:14] Lena Ortiz: Redwood standard is a single-signature MSA with order form executed by authorized signatories. Legal can accept countersigns but we prefer to keep MSA template and negotiate DPA redlines.

[24:30] Sarah Cole: Regarding billing attribution — can we get a token-level breakdown? Our FinOps wants per-product taggable invoices so we can attribute to teams.
[24:39] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we have token-level billing and per-route cost breakdowns in Console — you can export CSVs or connect to BI tools.

[25:55] Markus Lind: Any export controls or encryption clause that would force suspension of service if a jurisdiction is blocked? We need clarity on termination vs temporary restriction.
[26:05] Lena Ortiz: The MSA includes a force majeure/exports clause; operationally we aim for graceful restriction. We'll highlight those sections.

[27:40] Marcus Hale: One more technical note: if you choose Dedicated with multi-AZ replication, we can push SLA to 99.99 with a warm standby, but costs increase for the redundancy. We'll model that.

[29:02] Priya Nair: Ok procurement will need a clear table: commit level — monthly fee — included egress — SLA — service credits — termination notice.
[29:11] Lena Ortiz: We'll put that exact table in the pricing worksheet and MSA appendix.

[30:45] Jonas Meyer: For compliance, SOC2 attestation and ability for us to do a security assessment — do you allow a limited security assessment or an on-site audit?
[30:56] Lena Ortiz: We provide SOC2 Type II and ISO reports; for deeper reviews we can facilitate a security questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ) and discuss controlled assessments with our security team under NDA. On-site audits are rare but can be arranged under special terms.

[32:10] Sarah Cole: Any minimum notice for changing encryption keys? Key rotation windows?
[32:16] Marcus Hale: Key rotation is supported; we recommend scheduled rotation windows (monthly/quarterly). Emergency rotation is supported but requires our ops coordination; we'll record that in the runbook.

[33:45] Lena Ortiz: Let's talk timeline. Are you targeting pilot -> procurement approval in 30 days?
[33:53] Priya Nair: Ideally yes. Procurement wants pricing and legal redlines within 5-7 business days to route to approvers.

[34:10] Lena Ortiz: Action: we'll send annotated MSA/DPA by 8/8 and the pricing worksheet by 8/7. Marcus — benchmark scheduling?
[34:20] Marcus Hale: I'll propose slots 8/12 or 8/13 for a 2-hour benchmark window and a separate 4-hour longer run if needed.

[35:40] Markus Lind: For DPA exceptions: Atlas will probably request an SCC-only transfer model and a prohibition on US processing for certain data classes. We'll flag that.
[35:50] Lena Ortiz: Noted. We'll mark those as high-priority redlines.

[37:05] Jonas Meyer: About incident response time — can you commit to an initial response within 15 minutes for Sev1?
[37:12] Marcus Hale: Our standard is a 15-minute acknowledgment for Sev1 and a 1-hour mitigation update. We log all incidents in the Console and provide postmortems for Sev1s. We can formalize timing in the SLA appendix.

[38:35] Sarah Cole: A question from our infra — what's the expected data path for embeddings? Will embeddings be stored by Redwood by default?
[38:44] Marcus Hale: Embeddings storage is optional. We store embeddings for caching by default in hosted to speed up rerank/recall, but we can turn off persistent storage or forward embeddings to your storage endpoint. This is configurable in the privacy settings or DPA.

[40:02] Lena Ortiz: There's a pricing nuance — embeddings storage beyond Y GB/month may carry a small storage charge. We'll show that in the worksheet.

[41:35] Priya Nair: If we go annual committed, what are termination rights for material breach? Procurement wants clarity on pro-rated refunds and early termination penalties.
[41:44] Lena Ortiz: We can negotiate early termination clauses — standard is a 30-day cure period for breach, pro-rated refunds in limited scenarios, and termination for convenience with a notice and possible cancellation fee for reserved capacity. We'll mark that for legal.

[43:05] Markus Lind: We'll also request clarity on data deletion timing post-termination — max 30 days and certificate of deletion?
[43:12] Marcus Hale: We can commit to deletion within 30 days and provide a certificate of destruction for data in our hosted platform under the enterprise package. For Private deployments, you'd control deletion.

[44:30] Lena Ortiz: Any other blockers?
[44:36] Jonas Meyer: One small item — we need proof that operator IAM is segmented and that no single engineer can exfiltrate raw data.
[44:44] Marcus Hale: We enforce RBAC and MFA for operator accounts, with session recording for privileged ops. We'll include an architecture snippet showing separation of control plane and data plane keys.

[46:00] Priya Nair: Ok procurement will move once we get the MSA/DPA and the pricing table. We'll also want a sample order form structure to see approval fields.

[46:12] Lena Ortiz: We'll include a sample order form (shows line items, commit units, region, payment terms).

[47:30] Marcus Hale: One more technical note — the Dedicated topology includes an optional warm-fallback to hosted variants if capacity is exhausted. That can be done with a contractual routing preference and limits on fallback to control costs.

[48:02] Sarah Cole: If fallback happens, will data touch Redwood-hosted models not in our VPC?
[48:09] Marcus Hale: That depends on the routing policy — you can opt out of cross-tenant fallback. We'll document exact behavior and fallback telemetry.

[49:25] Lena Ortiz: All right final recap — action items and owners as discussed. Marcus will schedule benchmark and share harness; Lena will send annotated MSA/DPA and pricing workbook; Atlas legal/procurement to send priority redlines and audit retention requirements; follow-up legal sync and benchmark scheduling.

[50:00] Markus Lind: I'll aim to send prioritized redlines by Friday 8/8.
[50:06] Priya Nair: Procurement will look at the pricing sheet and come back with a committee date.

[51:10] Marcus Hale: For the benchmark, I'll include a short readme and a sanitized sample dataset. You'll be able to run locally or let Redwood run it in a dedicated window.

[52:30] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark slots and the legal sync. And we'll post the pricing spreadsheet link in a follow-up email — it's the single source of truth.

[53:15] Sarah Cole: Thanks — that should be enough for our approvers initially.
[53:20] Jonas Meyer: Thanks all.
[53:25] Lena Ortiz: Meeting adjourned.

References / shared artifacts mentioned: pricing worksheet (link to redwood.com/attachments/pricing-worksheet-aug2025), annotated MSA template (will be attached), benchmark harness (github link shared during follow-up).

Notes on transcript accuracy: Automatic transcription captured technical terms with occasional errors (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache; "S A L" spaced out). Speaker attributions verified to best-effort.

Recap (final): Redwood to supply annotated MSA/DPA + pricing worksheet; Redwood SE to run Dedicated benchmark with synthetic/anonymized data; Atlas to provide prioritized legal redlines and audit retention requirements; follow-up legal sync and benchmark scheduling.
